description: Evidence-led candidate clusters for observable desire events: blocked approach to an inaccessible target, immediate-reward versus long-term-goal conflict, repeated acquisition without use, accumulation beyond capacity, an overt claim toward another adult's owned object, unfair extra-share taking, a public recognition bid with audience response, pursuit of a next milestone, and acquisition of resource-control authority. Broad desire, longing, greed, ambition, power, envy, obsession, philosophical, religious, and clinical labels remain advisory by themselves.

visual_semantics.primary_visual_proposition: One adult makes an incomplete approach toward one identifiable target while a visible barrier or unbridgeable distance keeps the target inaccessible and leaves an immediate contact or entry gap.

The same adult faces a concrete immediate reward that conflicts with a marked longer-term goal, makes one visible resistance or enactment choice, and leaves a same-frame outcome on the rejected or interrupted path.
The same adult acquires another item from one category while several prior matching acquisitions remain visibly unopened or unused and already press on storage or attention.
An adult continues adding matching resources after a visible storage or use capacity is already full, causing physical overflow, displacement, or blockage in the same frame.

One adult makes an overt claim, exchange bid, or boundary-crossing reach toward a single object still visibly held or worn by another adult, whose protective or refusal response preserves the ownership boundary.
Inside one visible allocation system, an adult crosses the marked boundary of their own share and moves an extra assigned share away from another recipient, leaving a same-frame shortage.
An adult publicly presents a specific work, achievement, or role marker to an identifiable audience whose independent attention produces an immediate recognition result.
After one visible completed milestone, the same adult actively invests work or resources toward a distinct next milestone while current progress feedback connects the two states.
An adult visibly seeks or obtains control over one valued resource or access right and the resulting grant, withholding, blockage, or rerouting changes an identifiable affected person's access.
